hard_fails.actual: On the standalone/free cart (wpss_get_user_cart(), src/functions/services.php:1416-1453), when a service is PERMANENTLY deleted while it sits in a buyer's persistent cart, the item vanishes from the rendered cart with zero notice, zero line item, and zero total adjustment -- the buyer simply sees a smaller total and fewer items with no explanation. Reproduced live: as wpss_buyer_ella, added service 5161 ($25) to cart alongside service 242 ($75) via the real 'Continue to Checkout' add-to-cart flow (cart totalled $100.00, 2 items). Force-deleted service 5161 via wp-cli while it sat in the cart. Reloading /cart/ showed only service 242 at $75.00, 1 item -- the $25 item and any trace of it were completely absent from the page, with no 'no longer offered' message of any kind. The underlying _wpss_cart user-meta STILL carries the dead entry (confirmed via direct meta read) because the cart-page render path calls wpss_get_user_cart() with keep_paused=true, which never persists the removal, so the buyer also has no way to discover or clear the ghost row themselves. Root cause: inside wpss_get_user_cart(), the branch `if ( ! $service || ! $keep_paused ) { $changed = true; continue; }` unconditionally drops an item the moment get_post() returns null, before the keep_paused/notice logic that a merely-unpublished (still-existing) service gets can run -- by design per the function's own docblock ('Deleted services are always dropped - there is nothing to come back to'), but no notice mechanism exists anywhere in templates/cart/cart.php or the calling shortcode for this class of removal, unlike the unpublish case which correctly renders 'This service is not currently available.' This is the SAME defect class as the already-tracked wpss-cart-delete-no-notice card (10331371292-adjacent lineage), whose fix (wp-sell-services-pro 388984c, per docs/qa/accepted-findings.json) only reached the WooCommerce/Pro cart rail -- the Free/standalone cart, which is what every free-mode install actually runs, still silently drops deleted-service line items with no buyer-facing explanation.

top3: HARD FAIL (free/standalone rail): permanently deleting a service while it sits in a buyer's persistent cart makes the line item vanish from /cart/ with zero notice and zero total adjustment -- the buyer just sees a smaller total with no explanation, and the stale row is never cleaned from their _wpss_cart meta since the cart render path never persists removals. This is the free-mode twin of the already-tracked wpss-cart-delete-no-notice defect, whose only fix so far landed in wp-sell-services-pro (WooCommerce rail) -- the standalone rail every free install actually runs is still broken.

GOOD NEWS, re-verified and now closed: the free-only add-ons falsy-'0' bug from the prior free-mode walk (index-0 add-on silently dropped from checkout) is FIXED on this commit. Selecting Rush Delivery alone (index 0), Source Files alone (index 1), and both together on a 2-add-on service all price and persist correctly into wpss_orders (subtotal/addons_total/total/commission math all verified via direct DB reads on orders #859 and #860), and payment_method is 'offline', never NULL.

Moderate inconsistency (soft, not blocking): the publish-completeness gate protects the STATUS invariant correctly (an already-live incomplete service never gets silently unpublished -- confirmed via wp-cli field resave), but PUT /wpss/v1/services/{id} refuses the ENTIRE request (400 wpss_not_publishable) for ANY edit to an already-published-but-incomplete service, even a same-value title change with no status field in the payload. This is a deliberate documented trade-off in ServicesController.php (closing Basecamp 10320551446, a live-listing reprice-below-floor exploit) but it means a vendor cannot save even a trivial edit to a grandfathered incomplete listing through the REST-backed dashboard edit flow until they backfill everything the current rules demand.

failures.triage_note: Same defect class as the previously-tracked wpss-cart-delete-no-notice finding, but reproduced here specifically on the FREE/standalone cart rail, which the earlier fix (wp-sell-services-pro 388984c) did not touch. See hard_fails[] for full repro and root cause (src/functions/services.php wpss_get_user_cart(), templates/cart/cart.php has no notice path for a fully-deleted item).
failures.expected: Per the release's own spec (matching the unpublish-case behaviour already correct on this rail): when the underlying service is deleted, the item is removed from the cart with a visible notice saying it is no longer offered, the same way an unpublished service shows 'This service is not currently available.'
failures.actual: As wpss_buyer_ella: after force-deleting service 5161 while it sat in a 2-item cart ($100.00 total), /cart/ silently dropped to 1 item / $75.00 with no notice, no removed-item indicator, and no way to discover the still-present ghost row in _wpss_cart user meta.

failures.triage_note: ServicesController::update_item() (src/API/ServicesController.php:826-849) keys its publishability gate off the service's EFFECTIVE resulting status, not off whether the request touches status at all -- deliberately, per its own inline comment, to close a real prior exploit (Basecamp 10320551446: a live listing repriced below the $5 floor via a status-less PUT). The side effect: a live-but-incomplete service (creatable only by a pre-existing dataset, or by force-publish outside the wizard, since the wizard/REST publish gate itself is correctly enforced -- see PASS items) cannot be edited AT ALL via this REST route, including edits with nothing to do with completeness. A parallel, non-REST save path (wp-cli's wp_update_post(), and presumably the classic wp-admin 'Update' button on an already-published post) does NOT run this same gate and saves unrelated fields freely without touching status. The two save paths for editing the same object enforce different rules.
failures.expected: An already-live incomplete service stays live when an unrelated field is saved -- the STATUS invariant holds either way in this repro (it does), but a stricter reading of that promise is that the EDIT itself should also succeed for fields unrelated to completeness, matching what the wp-cli/save_post path already allows.
failures.actual: PUT /wpss/v1/services/5162 with only {"title": "..."} (no status field, post already publish) returned HTTP 400 wpss_not_publishable and did not apply the title change; a wp-cli `wp post update` changing the same field on the same post succeeded immediately and left status untouched.

failures.triage_note: Cosmetic/data-display issue only. Settings > Advanced renders 'Setup wizard was completed on January 1, 1970.' -- the classic Unix-epoch fallback (timestamp 0) formatted as if it were a real date, instead of a 'not yet run' / 'never completed' state. Low severity, but reads as a real (if implausible) completion date to a site owner.
failures.expected: When the setup-wizard-completed option has never been set, Settings > Advanced should say something like 'Setup wizard has not been run yet' rather than formatting timestamp 0 as a calendar date.
failures.actual: Settings > Advanced (System Settings section) literally reads 'Setup wizard was completed on January 1, 1970.'
